description: The best paint for cinder block starts with Loxon Block Surfacer, then 2 coats of acrylic masonry paint; 6 picks for dry, exterior and damp walls.
dek: The best paint for cinder block starts with Loxon Block Surfacer, then 2 coats of acrylic masonry paint; 6 picks for dry, exterior and damp walls.
intro: The best paint for cinder block is really a two-step system: one coat of a high-solids block filler such as Sherwin-Williams Loxon Block Surfacer, then two coats of a 100 percent acrylic masonry topcoat such as Behr Premium Masonry, Stucco and Brick Paint. If the wall is a damp basement wall, skip both and use a masonry waterproofer like DRYLOK Extreme instead.

Block takes paint, but not the way drywall does. Its face is full of pits, it is strongly alkaline, and below grade it is often wet from behind. Roll ordinary wall paint on it and you get pinholes, blotchy color that soaks up gallon after gallon, and flaking within a few seasons. Below are six products sorted by the layer they fill, then the questions that decide which ones your wall needs.
quickAnswer: On a dry interior or exterior block wall, apply one coat of block filler (Loxon Block Surfacer is the benchmark) and two coats of acrylic masonry paint (Behr Premium Masonry, or Loxon XP for a pro-grade exterior). On a damp basement wall, use two coats of a masonry waterproofer such as DRYLOK Extreme, Behr Basement and Masonry Waterproofer or, for mild dampness, KILZ.

blocks.p: Think in layers. The filler fixes texture, the topcoat gives color and weather resistance, and a waterproofer replaces both on a wall that gets wet from the soil side.

A dry garage or workshop wall needs filler plus topcoat. An above-grade exterior wall needs the same system with an exterior acrylic. A damp basement wall needs a waterproofer and, before that, a look at the drainage outside.

sections.h: The 6 Best Paints for Cinder Block in 2026, Ranked

blocks.p: These picks cover every layer of a block paint system. The order weighs what the makers publish (solids, alkali tolerance, coverage on block, moisture and pressure ratings, interior or exterior approval), how easy each is to buy, and recurring patterns in owner feedback. Specifications are attributed to their makers; none were measured by us.

blocks.h3: Best Block Filler: Sherwin-Williams Loxon Block Surfacer

blocks.p: Loxon Block Surfacer is the filler painters use when they want block to look smooth. It is a high-solids acrylic made to fill the voids and pits in a block face and leave a continuous, sealed surface for the topcoat. Sherwin-Williams builds the Loxon line for masonry, so it is formulated to tolerate the alkalinity of block and mortar that breaks down ordinary primers. It goes on heavy with a thick-nap roller, or by spray and back-roll, and covers far less area per gallon than a standard primer because much of it disappears into the block. That is exactly the point: once the pores are filled, two topcoats give even color instead of a pinholed, blotchy finish. It is approved inside and out and can be tinted toward the finish color. It is not a waterproofer.
**Pros:** fills block voids, built for alkaline masonry, tintable, interior and exterior, cuts topcoat use.
**Cons:** sold mainly at Sherwin-Williams stores, heavy to roll, low coverage on rough block.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Sherwin-Williams+Loxon+Block+Surfacer&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Topcoat: Behr Premium Masonry, Stucco and Brick Paint

blocks.p: This is a 100 percent acrylic topcoat made for the surfaces in its name, and it is the most practical finish coat for most people painting block. The acrylic binder stays flexible as the wall expands and contracts, tolerates the alkalinity of cement-based surfaces and holds up to sun and rain outdoors. It tints to a broad range of colors, and its low-sheen finish helps disguise block texture. It will go onto bare block, but it cannot fill voids, so put it over a coat of filler for a smooth result; two coats over filler is the normal spec. It is not for a basement wall with water coming through from behind. Owners commonly report good coverage and color retention on exterior block once the surface has been filled. It is easy to find at Home Depot.
**Pros:** 100 percent acrylic for masonry, exterior-rated, alkali resistant, wide colors, easy to buy.
**Cons:** needs filler underneath for best looks, not a waterproofer, flat finish is harder to scrub.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Behr+Premium+Masonry+Stucco+Brick+Paint&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best for Damp Basement Block: DRYLOK Extreme Masonry Waterproofer

blocks.p: When a basement block wall shows any dampness, filler and topcoat are the wrong products, and DRYLOK Extreme is built for that wall. It is a thick masonry waterproofer that the maker rates to withstand 15 psi of hydrostatic pressure when applied per the label, and it fills pores as it waterproofs, so on block it does the jobs of filler and moisture barrier at once. The first coat goes on with a stiff nylon brush, scrubbed in until no pinholes remain; the second follows after the label dry time. It comes in white and tints to lighter shades, and it can take a latex topcoat once cured. It needs bare masonry, free of paint, efflorescence and dirt, and it cannot stop water entering at the wall-floor joint.
**Pros:** published pressure rating, fills pores while waterproofing, works as the finish, tintable to light colors, mildew resistant.
**Cons:** limited colors and sheens, needs bare masonry, first coat must be brushed in.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=DRYLOK+Extreme+Masonry+Waterproofer&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Exterior Pro Grade: Sherwin-Williams Loxon XP

blocks.p: Loxon XP is Sherwin-Williams' contractor-grade exterior masonry coating, and it is the answer to queries about which Sherwin-Williams paint to put on an outside block wall or foundation. It is designed for concrete and masonry, formulated for alkaline surfaces and made to repel wind-driven rain while still letting the wall breathe. Sherwin-Williams publishes detailed data sheets covering surface pH limits, cure times and recommended primers, which makes it easier to build a system that lasts. On bare exterior block, apply it over Loxon Block Surfacer for a smooth finish; on a foundation that is partly painted and partly bare, spot-fill the bare block and use a compatible primer where the store staff recommend one. It keeps rain out from the outside and is not meant to resist water pushing through a basement wall from the soil side.
**Pros:** built for exterior masonry, alkali tolerant, sheds wind-driven rain, thorough data sheets, mildew resistant.
**Cons:** premium cost per gallon, sold mainly at Sherwin-Williams stores, not for interior basement waterproofing.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Sherwin-Williams+Loxon+XP+Masonry+Coating&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Waterproofer Alternative: Behr Premium Basement and Masonry Waterproofer

blocks.p: Behr's waterproofer is the main alternative to DRYLOK on the home-center shelf, and its wider tinting makes it appealing when you want a damp basement wall to look finished rather than plain white. It is a thick coating for unpainted concrete and masonry, block included, on interior and exterior walls. It works like other masonry waterproofers, filling pores and forming a continuous film, and Behr says it resists water pressure when applied as directed. Application matters as much as the product: clean to bare masonry, remove efflorescence, scrub the first coat in with a stiff brush, then apply a second. It will not stop water entering where the wall meets the floor or through a flowing crack. Owner feedback commonly mentions good results on damp block when prep is thorough.
**Pros:** made for basement and masonry walls, fills and seals porous block, tintable, widely available.
**Cons:** needs bare clean masonry, slow brush application, no fix for floor-joint leaks.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Behr+Premium+Basement+Masonry+Waterproofer&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Budget: KILZ Basement and Masonry Waterproofing Paint

blocks.p: KILZ's waterproofing paint is the budget choice for block that is damp but not actively seeping. It is made for unpainted concrete and masonry inside and out, fills the pores of block and leaves a continuous protective film. For a garage, a utility room or a basement wall that only darkens a little after heavy rain, it gives moisture protection and a clean finish for less money than the leading brands. Apply it the same way as any masonry waterproofer: strip old paint, remove efflorescence, brush the first coat hard into the block, then add a second after the label dry time. On a wall with visible seepage after every storm, the higher-rated products are worth the extra money, and drainage fixes matter more than any coating.
**Pros:** usually cheaper per gallon than rivals, interior and exterior, fills porous block, water cleanup.
**Cons:** lighter duty for wetter walls, few colors, needs bare masonry and careful brushing.

sections.h: What Kind of Paint Do You Use on Cinder Blocks?

blocks.p: Use a 100 percent acrylic masonry paint over a block filler on dry walls, and a masonry waterproofer on walls that get wet from behind. Ordinary interior wall paint fails on block for three separate reasons, and each layer of the system answers one.
The face of a block is covered in tiny voids. Thin latex bridges over them and leaves air pockets that show as pinholes. Block filler fills them.

Block, mortar and concrete are strongly alkaline, especially when new. Paints not made for masonry can suffer alkali burn, also called saponification, which leaves soft, discolored or flaking paint. Masonry primers and acrylic masonry paints are formulated for high pH.

Block absorbs and passes water. On a basement or retaining wall, water pushes on the film from behind and carries salts that deposit under it as efflorescence, so the paint blisters and peels. Drainage or a waterproofer solves that.

blocks.h3: Can you use regular acrylic latex on block?

blocks.p: A quality exterior acrylic latex labeled for masonry can work over a block filler on a dry wall. Read the can for masonry approval and alkali resistance. A standard interior wall paint is the wrong product, inside or out.

sections.h: Should You Prime Cinder Block Before Painting?

blocks.p: Yes. On bare block, the primer should be a block filler, a very thick, high-solids acrylic primer sometimes labeled block surfacer or masonry filler. It is the layer most people skip and the one that makes the biggest difference to the finished look.

blocks.h3: Why filler beats an ordinary primer

blocks.p: A standard primer is thin and bridges the voids the same way paint does. Filler goes on almost like a thin plaster, closes the pores and leaves a sealed surface. Bare block can absorb two or three topcoats before the color evens out and still show pinholes; one coat of filler closes the surface so two topcoats cover evenly. On a large wall, it often saves more topcoat than it costs.

Use a 3/4-inch nap roller for smooth block and up to 1-1/4-inch for rough or split-face block, loaded heavily, and work it into the surface so it fills rather than skims. Many painters spray it and back-roll. Expect about 50 to 100 square feet per gallon depending on texture; very porous block may need two coats.

Ask the store to tint the filler toward your topcoat color, which helps dark colors cover. Allow the full recoat time on the label; heavy filler dries more slowly than thin primer, especially in a cool basement.

sections.h: What Is the Best Paint for Cinder Block Basement Walls?

blocks.p: It depends on whether the wall is dry or damp, so test before you buy.

Tape an 18-inch square of clear plastic tightly to the bare wall and leave it 24 to 48 hours. Moisture on the wall side of the plastic means water is coming through the block. Moisture on the room side means humid air condensing on a cool wall. No moisture means the wall can take standard filler and topcoat.

Do not use ordinary paint. Fix what you can outside first: clean gutters, extend downspouts and regrade soil away from the wall. Then apply two coats of a masonry waterproofer such as DRYLOK Extreme. For walls that leak at the floor joint or through cracks, a coating is not enough; our guide to [basement waterproofing systems](/best-basement-waterproofing-systems/) covers drainage and sump options, and the [best basement wall sealer](/best-basement-wall-sealer/) guide compares coatings and penetrating sealers.

Run a dehumidifier to bring the room below 60 percent humidity, ideally 30 to 50 percent, before and after painting. Our picks for the [best dehumidifier for a basement](/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) handle the job.

White, chalky deposits mean moisture has been moving through the block. Brush them off dry, clean with an efflorescence remover, rinse and let the wall dry. If they return quickly, the moisture problem comes before any paint. Any mildew spots need treating first too; see the [best mold remover](/best-mold-remover/) guide.

sections.h: What Is the Best Paint for Cinder Block Exterior Walls?

blocks.p: A 100 percent acrylic exterior masonry paint over block filler, or an elastomeric masonry coating where the block cracks. Exterior block faces UV, rain, freeze-thaw and wind-driven water, so the topcoat must be exterior-rated, fade resistant and flexible.

Acrylic masonry paint breathes enough to let vapor out, resists alkali and UV and comes in every color. Elastomeric coatings are much thicker and stretch across hairline cracks, which suits block that cracks along mortar joints or sees big temperature swings. They breathe less, so keep them off walls with moisture coming from behind, such as retaining walls.

blocks.h3: Paint that will not flake in a hot, dry climate

blocks.p: In sunny regions such as Southern California, flaking on old block usually traces to chalky old paint, efflorescence or a topcoat that was never filled under. Wash and scrape back to sound material, prime bare spots with filler, and use a premium exterior acrylic like Loxon XP or Behr Premium Masonry. Avoid painting in direct midday sun.
Walls with soil behind them get water from both sides. A penetrating water repellent usually outlasts paint there.

sections.h: How Do You Paint Cinder Block That Has Been Painted Before?

blocks.p: Test the old paint, remove anything loose, fill the bare spots, then topcoat. Many foundations are part painted and part bare, and the system has to handle both.

Press duct tape firmly onto the old paint and rip it off. If paint comes away, the coating is failing and must be removed. If the tape comes off clean, the old paint is sound and can be cleaned, scuffed and repainted.

Use a wire brush, scraper or stripper, or on exterior walls a pressure washer used carefully so it does not erode mortar. A grinder with a wire cup wheel is fast but dusty; wear a respirator. If the paint might predate 1978, test for lead before sanding and follow EPA lead-safe practices if it is positive.

Wash with a masonry cleaner or mild detergent, rinse and let it dry. Spot-fill bare block with block filler and use a bonding primer over glossy old paint, then apply two topcoats over everything. Masonry waterproofers generally require bare masonry, so switching a painted basement wall to a waterproofer means stripping it first.

blocks.h3: Find the cause of repeat peeling

blocks.p: If paint keeps failing in the same spots, look for a leaking gutter, a downspout at the base of the wall, a crack or a cold corner that sweats. Paint fails where water is.

sections.h: How Long Should New Cinder Block Cure Before Painting?

blocks.p: Paint makers commonly ask for new block and mortar to cure about 28 to 30 days before coating, and some products specify longer. Fresh masonry holds a lot of construction water and is very alkaline, so early paint traps moisture and risks alkali burn and blistering.

Some masonry primers are formulated for high-pH surfaces and list a maximum pH on their data sheet, often in the 12 to 13 range. If you must paint early, use one of those and check a wetted area with pH strips.

New block often shows efflorescence in its first months as construction water works out. Let it appear, brush it off and clean with a masonry cleaner before painting. Painting over fresh salts sets up the classic failure where they push paint off from behind.

Footing drains, gutters, downspout extensions and grading that slopes away from the wall do more for a painted block wall than any coating. A wall with roof water dumping at its base will show damage whatever paint is on it.

sections.h: How Much Paint Does a Cinder Block Wall Need?

blocks.p: Much more than the can suggests, because a pitted block face has far more surface area than its flat dimensions. Plan on one coat of filler and two coats of topcoat as the normal specification.

A filler-plus-two-topcoats system usually needs about 5 to 10 gallons of filler and 4 to 5 gallons of topcoat. A two-coat waterproofer system on the same damp wall needs about 10 to 12 gallons. Always check the rates on your specific product.

Use a thick-nap roller and a stiff nylon brush for mortar joints and corners. An airless sprayer speeds up large walls, but back-roll the first coat so it is worked into the surface; our guide to the [best paint sprayer](/best-paint-sprayer/) covers models that handle thick masonry coatings.

Most acrylic masonry products want surface and air temperatures above about 50 degrees Fahrenheit, though some allow lower. Avoid midday sun, rain and evening dew outdoors, and keep indoor humidity down. Painting contractors commonly quote around $2 to $5 per square foot for filler and topcoat, more where stripping or waterproofing is involved.

mistakes: Topcoat alone bridges over the voids in block, leaving pinholes and blotchy color on a wall that keeps soaking up paint. One coat of high-solids filler worked in with a thick-nap roller closes the surface so two topcoats look even, and it usually saves topcoat.

Fresh block and mortar hold construction water and stay highly alkaline for weeks. Early paint traps that moisture and suffers alkali burn, showing as soft, discolored or peeling patches. Wait about 28 to 30 days, or use a primer rated for high-pH surfaces.
Putting regular paint on a damp basement wall

Standard paint on a wall with water coming through blisters and peels as moisture and salts push behind it. Run a plastic sheet test first. If the wall side gets wet, fix outside drainage and use a masonry waterproofer instead of filler and topcoat.

Interior wall paint is not built for UV, rain or freeze-thaw and chalks and fails quickly on exterior block. Use a 100 percent acrylic exterior masonry paint or an exterior elastomeric coating, over a compatible block filler or masonry primer.

The white salts on block keep forming as moisture moves through, and they will push any coating off from behind. Brush them off dry, clean with an efflorescence remover, rinse and let the wall dry. If they come back fast, solve the moisture before painting.
bottomLine: On any bare cinder block wall, the best paint job starts with a high-solids filler such as Sherwin-Williams Loxon Block Surfacer, followed by two coats of a 100 percent acrylic masonry paint like Behr Premium Masonry, or Loxon XP for a premium exterior. If a basement wall shows dampness, switch to two coats of a masonry waterproofer such as DRYLOK Extreme, Behr's waterproofer or KILZ for mild cases, and fix gutters and grading first. Let new block cure about a month, clear efflorescence and failing paint, and the finish will last instead of flaking.

faqs.q: What is the best paint for cinder block?
faqs.a: The best paint for cinder block is a system: one coat of high-solids block filler such as Sherwin-Williams Loxon Block Surfacer, then two coats of 100 percent acrylic masonry paint such as Behr Premium Masonry, Stucco and Brick Paint. For damp basement block, use a masonry waterproofer such as DRYLOK Extreme instead of filler and topcoat.

faqs.q: What is the best Sherwin-Williams paint for cinder block?
faqs.a: The best Sherwin-Williams products for cinder block are Loxon Block Surfacer as the first coat on bare block and Loxon XP as the exterior topcoat. Both are formulated for alkaline masonry. For a foundation that is partly painted, spot-fill the bare block, prime glossy old paint as the store recommends, then topcoat everything.

faqs.q: Should I prime cinder blocks before using regular paint?
faqs.a: Yes, you should prime cinder blocks before painting, and the primer should be a block filler rather than an ordinary thin primer. Filler closes the pores so the topcoat does not show pinholes or soak in unevenly. Also use a topcoat rated for masonry, since standard interior paint can fail on alkaline block.

faqs.q: What is the best paint for damp basement cinder blocks?
faqs.a: The best paint for damp basement cinder blocks is a masonry waterproofer such as DRYLOK Extreme, which its maker rates for 15 psi of hydrostatic pressure. Behr Basement and Masonry Waterproofer offers more colors, and KILZ suits mild dampness. Apply two coats to bare, clean block, and fix gutters and grading outside first.

faqs.q: Can you paint over efflorescence on cinder block?
faqs.a: No, you should not paint over efflorescence on cinder block. The white salts come from moisture moving through the wall and will push paint off from behind. Brush them off dry, clean with an efflorescence remover, rinse and let the wall dry. If the salts return quickly, solve the moisture problem before painting.

faqs.q: Is cinder block paint waterproof enough for a shower?
faqs.a: No, masonry paint or a basement waterproofer is not a substitute for a proper shower waterproofing system. Showers see constant direct water and steam, and a painted block wall will eventually fail there. Use a waterproofing membrane system designed for wet areas behind tile or panels, and follow its maker's instructions.

faqs.q: How many coats of paint does cinder block need?
faqs.a: Cinder block normally needs one coat of block filler and two coats of topcoat. Very porous or split-face block may need a second filler coat. Damp basement walls instead get two coats of masonry waterproofer, with the first scrubbed in by brush until no pinholes remain.
